---------------------------- MODULE W4Od7m3p0t2 ----------------------------
(* Two independent crane-control clusters share one loading berth. Each     *)
(* cluster elects a leader controller; only an alive leader may drive the   *)
(* berth. Leaders can fail and be replaced (failover); the berth is the     *)
(* single critical resource shared by both clusters.                        *)
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Controllers, ClusterA, NoCtrl, MaxTerm

ASSUME NoCtrl \notin Controllers
ASSUME ClusterA \subseteq Controllers

Instances == {"a", "b"}
Assign(c) == IF c \in ClusterA THEN "a" ELSE "b"
CtrlsOf(i) == {c \in Controllers : Assign(c) = i}

VARIABLES leader, alive, inBerth, term

vars == <<leader, alive, inBerth, term>>

TypeInv ==
    /\ leader \in [Instances -> Controllers \cup {NoCtrl}]
    /\ alive \in [Controllers -> BOOLEAN]
    /\ inBerth \subseteq Instances
    /\ term \in [Instances -> 0..MaxTerm]

Init ==
    /\ leader = [i \in Instances |-> NoCtrl]
    /\ alive = [c \in Controllers |-> TRUE]
    /\ inBerth = {}
    /\ term = [i \in Instances |-> 0]

Elect(i, c) ==
    /\ leader[i] = NoCtrl
    /\ c \in CtrlsOf(i)
    /\ alive[c]
    /\ term[i] < MaxTerm
    /\ leader' = [leader EXCEPT ![i] = c]
    /\ term' = [term EXCEPT ![i] = term[i] + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<alive, inBerth>>

FailLeader(i) ==
    /\ leader[i] # NoCtrl
    /\ alive' = [alive EXCEPT ![leader[i]] = FALSE]
    /\ leader' = [leader EXCEPT ![i] = NoCtrl]
    /\ inBerth' = inBerth \ {i}
    /\ UNCHANGED term

Recover(c) ==
    /\ ~alive[c]
    /\ alive' = [alive EXCEPT ![c] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, inBerth, term>>

Enter(i) ==
    /\ leader[i] # NoCtrl
    /\ alive[leader[i]]
    /\ inBerth = {}
    /\ inBerth' = {i}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, alive, term>>

Leave(i) ==
    /\ i \in inBerth
    /\ inBerth' = inBerth \ {i}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, alive, term>>

Next ==
    \/ \E i \in Instances, c \in Controllers : Elect(i, c)
    \/ \E i \in Instances : FailLeader(i)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : Recover(c)
    \/ \E i \in Instances : Enter(i)
    \/ \E i \in Instances : Leave(i)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

(* No two distinct clusters occupy the shared berth simultaneously, and     *)
(* only a still-alive elected leader can be occupying it.                    *)
BerthExclusion ==
    /\ \A i, j \in Instances : (i \in inBerth /\ j \in inBerth) => i = j
    /\ \A i \in inBerth : leader[i] # NoCtrl /\ alive[leader[i]]

=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Controllers = {c1, c2, c3, c4}
    ClusterA = {c1, c2}
    NoCtrl = noc
    MaxTerm = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT BerthExclusion
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A container-ship crane yard is run by two independent controller clusters that share a single loading berth, which is the only spot where a crane may transfer a container. Each cluster runs a small pool of controllers and, at any moment, designates one of them as its leader through a leader-election step. Only the current leader of a cluster is permitted to move that cluster's crane into the shared berth. A leader can crash at any time; when it does, the cluster loses its leader and any berth occupancy it held is dropped, after which a surviving controller in the same cluster can be elected as the new leader (failover). A crashed controller may later recover and become eligible again. Because both clusters draw on the same physical berth, they must never both be using it at the same instant. Elections are bounded by a fixed number of terms so the system settles.
SAFETY PROPERTY: At any reachable state, at most one of the two clusters occupies the shared berth, and whichever cluster occupies it does so through a controller that is currently its elected, still-alive leader.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od0m2p2t2 ----------------------------
(* Two OR-scheduling coordinators share one pool of operating-room time     *)
(* blocks. Each surgery reservation runs as a two-phase commit: a block is  *)
(* escrowed, participating departments vote, and the transaction either     *)
(* commits (block allocated) or aborts (block returned). No time block is   *)
(* ever created or lost.                                                     *)
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Departments, Txns, TotalBlocks

VARIABLES phase, yesVoters, freeBlocks, escrowed, allocated

vars == <<phase, yesVoters, freeBlocks, escrowed, allocated>>

TypeInv ==
    /\ phase \in [Txns -> {"idle", "voting", "committed", "aborted"}]
    /\ yesVoters \in [Txns -> SUBSET Departments]
    /\ freeBlocks \in 0..TotalBlocks
    /\ escrowed \in 0..TotalBlocks
    /\ allocated \in 0..TotalBlocks

Init ==
    /\ phase = [t \in Txns |-> "idle"]
    /\ yesVoters = [t \in Txns |-> {}]
    /\ freeBlocks = TotalBlocks
    /\ escrowed = 0
    /\ allocated = 0

Begin(t) ==
    /\ phase[t] = "idle"
    /\ freeBlocks >= 1
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![t] = "voting"]
    /\ freeBlocks' = freeBlocks - 1
    /\ escrowed' = escrowed + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<yesVoters, allocated>>

Vote(t, d) ==
    /\ phase[t] = "voting"
    /\ d \in Departments
    /\ yesVoters' = [yesVoters EXCEPT ![t] = yesVoters[t] \cup {d}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, freeBlocks, escrowed, allocated>>

Commit(t) ==
    /\ phase[t] = "voting"
    /\ yesVoters[t] = Departments
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![t] = "committed"]
    /\ escrowed' = escrowed - 1
    /\ allocated' = allocated + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<yesVoters, freeBlocks>>

Abort(t) ==
    /\ phase[t] = "voting"
    /\ yesVoters[t] # Departments
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![t] = "aborted"]
    /\ escrowed' = escrowed - 1
    /\ freeBlocks' = freeBlocks + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<yesVoters, allocated>>

Next ==
    \/ \E t \in Txns : Begin(t)
    \/ \E t \in Txns, d \in Departments : Vote(t, d)
    \/ \E t \in Txns : Commit(t)
    \/ \E t \in Txns : Abort(t)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

(* Across both coordinators sharing the pool, the total number of time      *)
(* blocks is invariant: free + tentatively-escrowed + allocated is always   *)
(* exactly the fixed pool size.                                             *)
BlockConservation == freeBlocks + escrowed + allocated = TotalBlocks

=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Departments = {anes, nurse}
    Txns = {t1, t2, t3}
    TotalBlocks = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT BlockConservation
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A hospital runs two independent operating-room scheduling coordinators that draw from one shared pool of operating-room time blocks. When a surgery is booked, the reservation proceeds as a two-phase commit: first a single time block is taken out of the free pool and held in escrow for the transaction, then the participating departments (anesthesiology and nursing) each cast a vote. If every department votes yes, the transaction commits and its escrowed block becomes permanently allocated. If any department declines, the transaction aborts and its escrowed block is returned to the free pool. Several transactions, owned by either coordinator, can be in flight at once, but they all share the same finite pool of blocks. Blocks are never conjured from nothing and never silently discarded; every block is always either free, escrowed by an in-flight transaction, or allocated to a committed one.
SAFETY PROPERTY: In every reachable state the sum of free, escrowed, and allocated time blocks equals the fixed total pool size, so no block is ever created or destroyed.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od9m0p0t4 ----------------------------
(* A power-grid load shedder. Controllers use optimistic locking to enter   *)
(* the critical shedding section on a grid segment: read the segment's      *)
(* version, then commit only if the version is unchanged and the section is *)
(* clear; a stale read forces a retry. Available shed capacity (budget)     *)
(* changes at runtime.                                                       *)
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Controllers, Segments, MaxVer, MaxBudget

VARIABLES version, cstate, readVer, target, inSection, budget

vars == <<version, cstate, readVer, target, inSection, budget>>

TypeInv ==
    /\ version \in [Segments -> 0..MaxVer]
    /\ cstate \in [Controllers -> {"idle", "read", "applying"}]
    /\ readVer \in [Controllers -> 0..MaxVer]
    /\ target \in [Controllers -> Segments]
    /\ inSection \in [Segments -> SUBSET Controllers]
    /\ budget \in 0..MaxBudget

Init ==
    /\ version = [s \in Segments |-> 0]
    /\ cstate = [c \in Controllers |-> "idle"]
    /\ readVer = [c \in Controllers |-> 0]
    /\ target = [c \in Controllers |-> CHOOSE s \in Segments : TRUE]
    /\ inSection = [s \in Segments |-> {}]
    /\ budget = MaxBudget

Read(c, s) ==
    /\ cstate[c] = "idle"
    /\ cstate' = [cstate EXCEPT ![c] = "read"]
    /\ readVer' = [readVer EXCEPT ![c] = version[s]]
    /\ target' = [target EXCEPT ![c] = s]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, inSection, budget>>

Enter(c) ==
    /\ cstate[c] = "read"
    /\ LET s == target[c] IN
        /\ version[s] = readVer[c]
        /\ inSection[s] = {}
        /\ budget >= 1
        /\ version[s] < MaxVer
        /\ inSection' = [inSection EXCEPT ![s] = {c}]
        /\ version' = [version EXCEPT ![s] = version[s] + 1]
    /\ cstate' = [cstate EXCEPT ![c] = "applying"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<readVer, target, budget>>

Retry(c) ==
    /\ cstate[c] = "read"
    /\ version[target[c]] # readVer[c]
    /\ cstate' = [cstate EXCEPT ![c] = "idle"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, readVer, target, inSection, budget>>

Exit(c) ==
    /\ cstate[c] = "applying"
    /\ LET s == target[c] IN
        inSection' = [inSection EXCEPT ![s] = inSection[s] \ {c}]
    /\ cstate' = [cstate EXCEPT ![c] = "idle"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, readVer, target, budget>>

RaiseCap ==
    /\ budget < MaxBudget
    /\ budget' = budget + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, cstate, readVer, target, inSection>>

LowerCap ==
    /\ budget > 0
    /\ budget' = budget - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, cstate, readVer, target, inSection>>

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Controllers, s \in Segments : Read(c, s)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : Enter(c)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : Retry(c)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : Exit(c)
    \/ RaiseCap
    \/ LowerCap

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

(* Never do two controllers occupy the shedding critical section of the     *)
(* same grid segment at once.                                               *)
ExclusiveShedAccess ==
    \A s \in Segments :
        \A c1, c2 \in inSection[s] : c1 = c2

=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Controllers = {x, y}
    Segments = {s1, s2}
    MaxVer = 2
    MaxBudget = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT ExclusiveShedAccess
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A power-grid load shedder coordinates several controllers that each want to apply a shedding command to a grid segment. Access uses optimistic locking with retry: a controller first reads the current version number of a segment, remembering the value it saw. To actually enter the critical shedding section it must find that the segment's version is still exactly what it read, that no other controller is already in that segment's section, and that some shed budget remains; on success it enters, bumping the segment's version. If, when it tries, the version has moved on because someone else acted, its optimistic read is stale and it abandons the attempt and retries from the beginning. When a controller finishes it leaves the section. Meanwhile the total available shed capacity rises and falls at runtime as grid conditions change. The shedding section of any one segment is a critical resource.
SAFETY PROPERTY: For every grid segment, at most one controller is inside that segment's shedding critical section at any time.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od8m0p6t4 ----------------------------
(* A university course-registration system using optimistic locking with    *)
(* retry. A student reads the current registration epoch (a version stamp)  *)
(* when it starts holding a seat, and may only commit an enrollment while    *)
(* that stamp is still current. The registrar reconfigures capacity at      *)
(* runtime, which advances the epoch; already-committed enrollments are     *)
(* re-stamped (they remain authorized) while in-flight holders go stale and *)
(* must retry.                                                               *)
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Students, MaxSeats, MaxEpoch

VARIABLES capacity, seatEpoch, enrolled, sstate, token

vars == <<capacity, seatEpoch, enrolled, sstate, token>>

TypeInv ==
    /\ capacity \in 0..MaxSeats
    /\ seatEpoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
    /\ enrolled \subseteq Students
    /\ sstate \in [Students -> {"idle", "holding", "enrolled"}]
    /\ token \in [Students -> 0..MaxEpoch]

Init ==
    /\ capacity = MaxSeats
    /\ seatEpoch = 0
    /\ enrolled = {}
    /\ sstate = [s \in Students |-> "idle"]
    /\ token = [s \in Students |-> 0]

Browse(s) ==
    /\ sstate[s] = "idle"
    /\ sstate' = [sstate EXCEPT ![s] = "holding"]
    /\ token' = [token EXCEPT ![s] = seatEpoch]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<capacity, seatEpoch, enrolled>>

Enroll(s) ==
    /\ sstate[s] = "holding"
    /\ token[s] = seatEpoch
    /\ s \notin enrolled
    /\ Cardinality(enrolled) < capacity
    /\ enrolled' = enrolled \cup {s}
    /\ sstate' = [sstate EXCEPT ![s] = "enrolled"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<capacity, seatEpoch, token>>

Retry(s) ==
    /\ sstate[s] = "holding"
    /\ token[s] # seatEpoch
    /\ sstate' = [sstate EXCEPT ![s] = "idle"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<capacity, seatEpoch, enrolled, token>>

Reconfigure(newcap) ==
    /\ seatEpoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ newcap \in 0..MaxSeats
    /\ seatEpoch' = seatEpoch + 1
    /\ capacity' = newcap
    /\ token' = [s \in Students |-> IF s \in enrolled THEN seatEpoch + 1 ELSE token[s]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<enrolled, sstate>>

Next ==
    \/ \E s \in Students : Browse(s)
    \/ \E s \in Students : Enroll(s)
    \/ \E s \in Students : Retry(s)
    \/ \E newcap \in 0..MaxSeats : Reconfigure(newcap)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

(* Every committed enrollment was made against the current registration     *)
(* epoch: no student holding a stale version stamp is ever counted as       *)
(* enrolled.                                                                 *)
OnlyFreshEnrollments == \A s \in enrolled : token[s] = seatEpoch

=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Students = {a, b}
    MaxSeats = 2
    MaxEpoch = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT OnlyFreshEnrollments
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A university course-registration system lets students compete for a limited number of seats using optimistic locking with retry. When a student begins holding a seat, it reads and remembers the current registration epoch, a version stamp that the registrar advances whenever it reconfigures capacity. A student may finalize its enrollment only while the stamp it remembered still matches the current epoch and a seat remains; committing adds it to the enrolled set. If the registrar has since reconfigured capacity, an in-flight holder's remembered stamp is now stale, so it must abandon the attempt and retry from the start. When the registrar reconfigures the number of seats at runtime, the epoch advances; students already fully enrolled are re-stamped to the new epoch and stay authorized, but merely-holding students are left stale. No enrollment is ever completed on the basis of an out-of-date view of the course.
SAFETY PROPERTY: In every reachable state, every student counted as enrolled carries the current registration epoch stamp, so no stale, unauthorized enrollment is ever recorded.

--------------------------- MODULE W4Od14m6p0t4 ---------------------------
(* A wildfire drone surveillance swarm. Drones take time-limited leases on  *)
(* survey sectors; only the current, unexpired lease-holder may actively    *)
(* survey a sector. Leases expire as a global clock advances. The set of    *)
(* active drones in the swarm changes at runtime as drones join and leave.  *)
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Drones, Sectors, NoDrone, LeaseLen, MaxTime

ASSUME NoDrone \notin Drones

VARIABLES clock, lease, expiry, active, surveying

vars == <<clock, lease, expiry, active, surveying>>

TypeInv ==
    /\ clock \in 0..MaxTime
    /\ lease \in [Sectors -> Drones \cup {NoDrone}]
    /\ expiry \in [Sectors -> 0..MaxTime]
    /\ active \subseteq Drones
    /\ surveying \in [Sectors -> SUBSET Drones]

Init ==
    /\ clock = 0
    /\ lease = [s \in Sectors |-> NoDrone]
    /\ expiry = [s \in Sectors |-> 0]
    /\ active = Drones
    /\ surveying = [s \in Sectors |-> {}]

Acquire(d, s) ==
    /\ d \in active
    /\ surveying[s] = {}
    /\ (lease[s] = NoDrone \/ clock >= expiry[s])
    /\ clock + LeaseLen <= MaxTime
    /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT ![s] = d]
    /\ expiry' = [expiry EXCEPT ![s] = clock + LeaseLen]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, active, surveying>>

Survey(d, s) ==
    /\ lease[s] = d
    /\ clock < expiry[s]
    /\ surveying[s] = {}
    /\ surveying' = [surveying EXCEPT ![s] = {d}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, lease, expiry, active>>

StopSurvey(d, s) ==
    /\ d \in surveying[s]
    /\ surveying' = [surveying EXCEPT ![s] = surveying[s] \ {d}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, lease, expiry, active>>

Expire(s) ==
    /\ lease[s] # NoDrone
    /\ clock >= expiry[s]
    /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT ![s] = NoDrone]
    /\ surveying' = [surveying EXCEPT ![s] = {}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, expiry, active>>

Tick ==
    /\ clock < MaxTime
    /\ clock' = clock + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lease, expiry, active, surveying>>

Depart(d) ==
    /\ d \in active
    /\ active' = active \ {d}
    /\ lease' = [s \in Sectors |-> IF lease[s] = d THEN NoDrone ELSE lease[s]]
    /\ surveying' = [s \in Sectors |-> surveying[s] \ {d}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, expiry>>

Rejoin(d) ==
    /\ d \notin active
    /\ active' = active \cup {d}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, lease, expiry, surveying>>

Next ==
    \/ \E d \in Drones, s \in Sectors : Acquire(d, s)
    \/ \E d \in Drones, s \in Sectors : Survey(d, s)
    \/ \E d \in Drones, s \in Sectors : StopSurvey(d, s)
    \/ \E s \in Sectors : Expire(s)
    \/ Tick
    \/ \E d \in Drones : Depart(d)
    \/ \E d \in Drones : Rejoin(d)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

(* Each sector is surveyed by at most one drone at a time, and any drone    *)
(* surveying a sector holds that sector's current, unexpired lease.         *)
SoleSurveyor ==
    \A s \in Sectors :
        /\ \A d1, d2 \in surveying[s] : d1 = d2
        /\ \A d \in surveying[s] : lease[s] = d

=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Drones = {d1, d2}
    Sectors = {s1, s2}
    NoDrone = none
    LeaseLen = 1
    MaxTime = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT SoleSurveyor
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A wildfire drone surveillance swarm divides the fire zone into survey sectors that individual drones must cover. Ownership of a sector is granted through a time-limited lease: a drone acquires a lease on a sector, stamped with an expiry time computed from a global clock, and only the current lease-holder whose lease has not yet expired may actively survey that sector. A drone can start and stop surveying while it holds a valid lease. As the global clock ticks forward, leases reach their expiry; an expired lease is released so the sector becomes available again. A drone may only take a sector that is free or whose lease has expired and that no one is actively surveying. The number of drones active in the swarm changes at runtime as drones depart (dropping any leases and surveys they held) and later rejoin. Because two drones surveying the same sector would collide, sector surveying is treated as a critical resource.
SAFETY PROPERTY: For every sector, at most one drone is actively surveying it at any moment, and any surveying drone is the current holder of that sector's lease.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od2m2p2t2 ----------------------------
(* A warehouse robot fleet moves crates between bins. Two robot             *)
(* coordinators share one pool of crates. Each crate move runs as a         *)
(* two-phase commit: a crate leaves its source bin into transit escrow,     *)
(* robots acknowledge, then the move commits (crate lands in the            *)
(* destination) or aborts (crate returns to source). Crates are conserved.  *)
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Bins, Txns, Robots

RECURSIVE Sigma(_, _)
Sigma(f, S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET x == CHOOSE y \in S : TRUE IN f[x] + Sigma(f, S \ {x})

TotalCrates == Cardinality(Bins)

VARIABLES content, tstate, escrow, src, dst, acks

vars == <<content, tstate, escrow, src, dst, acks>>

TypeInv ==
    /\ content \in [Bins -> 0..TotalCrates]
    /\ tstate \in [Txns -> {"idle", "prepared", "committed", "aborted"}]
    /\ escrow \in [Txns -> 0..1]
    /\ src \in [Txns -> Bins]
    /\ dst \in [Txns -> Bins]
    /\ acks \in [Txns -> SUBSET Robots]

Init ==
    /\ content = [b \in Bins |-> 1]
    /\ tstate = [t \in Txns |-> "idle"]
    /\ escrow = [t \in Txns |-> 0]
    /\ src = [t \in Txns |-> CHOOSE b \in Bins : TRUE]
    /\ dst = [t \in Txns |-> CHOOSE b \in Bins : TRUE]
    /\ acks = [t \in Txns |-> {}]

Begin(t, a, b) ==
    /\ tstate[t] = "idle"
    /\ a # b
    /\ content[a] >= 1
    /\ tstate' = [tstate EXCEPT ![t] = "prepared"]
    /\ content' = [content EXCEPT ![a] = content[a] - 1]
    /\ escrow' = [escrow EXCEPT ![t] = 1]
    /\ src' = [src EXCEPT ![t] = a]
    /\ dst' = [dst EXCEPT ![t] = b]
    /\ UNCHANGED acks

Ack(t, r) ==
    /\ tstate[t] = "prepared"
    /\ acks' = [acks EXCEPT ![t] = acks[t] \cup {r}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<content, tstate, escrow, src, dst>>

Commit(t) ==
    /\ tstate[t] = "prepared"
    /\ acks[t] = Robots
    /\ tstate' = [tstate EXCEPT ![t] = "committed"]
    /\ content' = [content EXCEPT ![dst[t]] = content[dst[t]] + 1]
    /\ escrow' = [escrow EXCEPT ![t] = 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<src, dst, acks>>

Abort(t) ==
    /\ tstate[t] = "prepared"
    /\ acks[t] # Robots
    /\ tstate' = [tstate EXCEPT ![t] = "aborted"]
    /\ content' = [content EXCEPT ![src[t]] = content[src[t]] + 1]
    /\ escrow' = [escrow EXCEPT ![t] = 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<src, dst, acks>>

Next ==
    \/ \E t \in Txns, a \in Bins, b \in Bins : Begin(t, a, b)
    \/ \E t \in Txns, r \in Robots : Ack(t, r)
    \/ \E t \in Txns : Commit(t)
    \/ \E t \in Txns : Abort(t)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

(* The crates in bins plus the crates held in transit escrow always sum to  *)
(* the fixed fleet total: no crate is manufactured or lost by a move.       *)
CrateConservation ==
    Sigma(content, Bins) + Sigma(escrow, Txns) = TotalCrates

=============================================================================
nl:
A warehouse robot fleet shuttles crates between storage bins under two independent robot coordinators that share one common pool of crates. Relocating a crate is done as a two-phase commit. In the first phase the crate is removed from its source bin and held in transit escrow for the move, and the move records its chosen source and destination bins. The participating robots then acknowledge the move one by one. Once every robot has acknowledged, the move commits and the crate is deposited into its destination bin. If the move cannot gather all acknowledgements it aborts, and the escrowed crate is put back into its source bin. Many moves can be in flight at once across both coordinators, but they all operate on the same finite population of crates. A crate is never duplicated and never vanishes: at every instant it is sitting in some bin or being held in transit for exactly one move.
SAFETY PROPERTY: In every reachable state, the number of crates resting in bins plus the number held in transit escrow equals the fixed total number of crates, so crates are neither created nor destroyed.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od7m4p0t1 ----------------------------
(* A container-ship crane yard buffers lift jobs in a bounded work queue     *)
(* with backpressure: when the queue is full new jobs are rejected. Queued  *)
(* jobs may be started in any order (messages can be reordered). The crane  *)
(* spreader is a critical resource: only one job may be on it at a time.    *)
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Jobs, MaxQ

VARIABLES pending, onSpreader, completed, rejected

vars == <<pending, onSpreader, completed, rejected>>

Placed == pending \cup onSpreader \cup completed \cup rejected

TypeInv ==
    /\ pending \subseteq Jobs
    /\ onSpreader \subseteq Jobs
    /\ completed \subseteq Jobs
    /\ rejected \subseteq Jobs

Init ==
    /\ pending = {}
    /\ onSpreader = {}
    /\ completed = {}
    /\ rejected = {}

Submit(j) ==
    /\ j \notin Placed
    /\ Cardinality(pending) < MaxQ
    /\ pending' = pending \cup {j}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<onSpreader, completed, rejected>>

Reject(j) ==
    /\ j \notin Placed
    /\ Cardinality(pending) = MaxQ

    /\ onSpreader' = {j}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<completed, rejected>>

Finish(j) ==

    /\ onSpreader' = onSpreader \ {j}

(* A power-grid load shedder guarded by hierarchical locks. To shed a       *)
(* feeder an operator must first take the coarse region lock, then the fine *)
(* feeder lock; only while holding both may it perform the shed action. An  *)
(* operator may be slow (it stalls while holding its locks) but does not    *)
(* fail. No operator ever sheds a feeder it is not fully authorized to.     *)
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Ops, Feeders, RegionNorthFeeders, NoOp, NoFeeder

ASSUME RegionNorthFeeders \subseteq Feeders
ASSUME NoOp \notin Ops
ASSUME NoFeeder \notin Feeders

Regions == {"rn", "rs"}
FeederRegion(f) == IF f \in RegionNorthFeeders THEN "rn" ELSE "rs"

VARIABLES regionLock, feederLock, opphase, actingFeeder

vars == <<regionLock, feederLock, opphase, actingFeeder>>

TypeInv ==
    /\ regionLock \in [Regions -> Ops \cup {NoOp}]
    /\ feederLock \in [Feeders -> Ops \cup {NoOp}]
    /\ opphase \in [Ops -> {"idle", "region", "feeder", "slow", "acting"}]
    /\ actingFeeder \in [Ops -> Feeders \cup {NoFeeder}]

Init ==
    /\ regionLock = [r \in Regions |-> NoOp]
    /\ feederLock = [f \in Feeders |-> NoOp]
    /\ opphase = [o \in Ops |-> "idle"]
    /\ actingFeeder = [o \in Ops |-> NoFeeder]

AcquireRegion(o, r) ==
    /\ opphase[o] = "idle"
    /\ regionLock[r] = NoOp
    /\ regionLock' = [regionLock EXCEPT ![r] = o]
    /\ opphase' = [opphase EXCEPT ![o] = "region"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<feederLock, actingFeeder>>

AcquireFeeder(o, f) ==
    /\ opphase[o] = "region"
    /\ regionLock[FeederRegion(f)] = o
    /\ feederLock[f] = NoOp
    /\ feederLock' = [feederLock EXCEPT ![f] = o]
    /\ opphase' = [opphase EXCEPT ![o] = "feeder"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<regionLock, actingFeeder>>

GoSlow(o) ==
    /\ opphase[o] = "feeder"
    /\ opphase' = [opphase EXCEPT ![o] = "slow"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<regionLock, feederLock, actingFeeder>>

Act(o, f) ==
    /\ opphase[o] \in {"feeder", "slow"}
    /\ feederLock[f] = o
    /\ regionLock[FeederRegion(f)] = o
    /\ opphase' = [opphase EXCEPT ![o] = "acting"]
    /\ actingFeeder' = [actingFeeder EXCEPT ![o] = f]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<regionLock, feederLock>>

Release(o) ==
    /\ opphase[o] = "acting"
    /\ LET f == actingFeeder[o] IN
        /\ feederLock' = [feederLock EXCEPT ![f] = NoOp]
        /\ regionLock' = [regionLock EXCEPT ![FeederRegion(f)] = NoOp]
    /\ opphase' = [opphase EXCEPT ![o] = "idle"]
    /\ actingFeeder' = [actingFeeder EXCEPT ![o] = NoFeeder]

Next ==
    \/ \E o \in Ops, r \in Regions : AcquireRegion(o, r)
    \/ \E o \in Ops, f \in Feeders : AcquireFeeder(o, f)
    \/ \E o \in Ops : GoSlow(o)
    \/ \E o \in Ops, f \in Feeders : Act(o, f)
    \/ \E o \in Ops : Release(o)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

(* Any operator currently shedding a feeder holds both that feeder's fine   *)
(* lock and the coarse lock of the feeder's region.                         *)
OnlyLockHoldersShed ==
    \A o \in Ops :
        opphase[o] = "acting" =>
            LET f == actingFeeder[o] IN
                /\ feederLock[f] = o
                /\ regionLock[FeederRegion(f)] = o

=============================================================================

A power-grid load shedder lets a few operators shed load on individual feeders, but every shed action is protected by two nested locks. An operator must first take the coarse lock on a whole region, and only then may it take the fine lock on a specific feeder inside that region, and only if that feeder lock is free. Holding both locks, the operator performs the actual shed action on the feeder. An operator may become slow, stalling for a while, but it never fails outright; it keeps holding its locks the whole time, so a slow operator simply delays others rather than breaking the protocol. When the operator is done it releases both the feeder lock and the region lock. The system must guarantee that a shed action is only ever performed by an operator that genuinely holds the proper authorization: no operator acts on a feeder without currently holding both that feeder's fine lock and the coarse lock of the feeder's region.
SAFETY PROPERTY: In every reachable state, any operator that is currently shedding a feeder holds both that feeder's fine lock and the coarse lock of the feeder's region.

--------------------------- MODULE W4Od10m8p4t0 ---------------------------
(* A subway signalling block system. Trains use hierarchical locks: first   *)
(* they acquire coarse admission to a line (bounded by that line's platform *)
(* capacity), then a fine per-block lock before running. A train can crash  *)
(* silently, vanishing while still holding its admission and block, which   *)
(* is never released -- yet the line capacity bound must never be exceeded. *)
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Trains, Blocks, LineABlocks, LineCap, NoTrain

ASSUME LineABlocks \subseteq Blocks
ASSUME NoTrain \notin Trains

Lines == {"la", "lb"}
BlockLine(b) == IF b \in LineABlocks THEN "la" ELSE "lb"

VARIABLES inLine, blockOcc, phase, crashed

vars == <<inLine, blockOcc, phase, crashed>>

TypeInv ==
    /\ inLine \in [Lines -> SUBSET Trains]
    /\ blockOcc \in [Blocks -> Trains \cup {NoTrain}]
    /\ phase \in [Trains -> {"out", "admitted", "running"}]
    /\ crashed \subseteq Trains

Init ==
    /\ inLine = [ln \in Lines |-> {}]
    /\ blockOcc = [b \in Blocks |-> NoTrain]
    /\ phase = [tr \in Trains |-> "out"]
    /\ crashed = {}

AcquireCoarse(tr, ln) ==
    /\ tr \notin crashed
    /\ phase[tr] = "out"
    /\ Cardinality(inLine[ln]) < LineCap
    /\ inLine' = [inLine EXCEPT ![ln] = inLine[ln] \cup {tr}]
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![tr] = "admitted"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<blockOcc, crashed>>

AcquireFine(tr, blk) ==
    /\ tr \notin crashed
    /\ phase[tr] = "admitted"
    /\ tr \in inLine[BlockLine(blk)]
    /\ blockOcc[blk] = NoTrain
    /\ blockOcc' = [blockOcc EXCEPT ![blk] = tr]
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![tr] = "running"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<inLine, crashed>>

Release(tr, blk) ==
    /\ tr \notin crashed
    /\ phase[tr] = "running"
    /\ blockOcc[blk] = tr
    /\ blockOcc' = [blockOcc EXCEPT ![blk] = NoTrain]
    /\ inLine' = [inLine EXCEPT ![BlockLine(blk)] = inLine[BlockLine(blk)] \ {tr}]
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![tr] = "out"]
    /\ UNCHANGED crashed

CrashSilently(tr) ==
    /\ tr \notin crashed
    /\ phase[tr] # "out"
    /\ crashed' = crashed \cup {tr}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<inLine, blockOcc, phase>>

Next ==
    \/ \E tr \in Trains, ln \in Lines : AcquireCoarse(tr, ln)
    \/ \E tr \in Trains, blk \in Blocks : AcquireFine(tr, blk)
    \/ \E tr \in Trains, blk \in Blocks : Release(tr, blk)
    \/ \E tr \in Trains : CrashSilently(tr)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

(* No line ever admits more trains than its platform capacity, even though  *)
(* silently-crashed trains hold their admission forever.                    *)
BoundedLineCapacity ==
    \A ln \in Lines : Cardinality(inLine[ln]) <= LineCap

=============================================================================
nl:
A subway signalling block system controls how trains move through the network using two levels of locking. Before a train may run, it must first take a coarse lock: admission to a whole line, which is granted only while that line holds fewer trains than its platform capacity. Having been admitted to a line, the train then takes a fine lock on a specific signalling block within that line, which it may do only if that block is currently unoccupied. Once it holds both, the train is running in its block. When it finishes, it releases the block and gives up its line admission. A train can crash silently: it simply vanishes while still admitted to its line and holding its block, and because the failure is silent, that admission and block are never released and continue to count against the line. Despite such leaked admissions, the line-capacity limit must always be respected.
SAFETY PROPERTY: In every reachable state, the number of trains admitted to any line never exceeds that line's platform capacity.

(* A pharmacy prescription dispenser. Each dispense request must gather a    *)
(* quorum of pharmacist approvals before a unit is reserved against stock    *)
(* and then dispensed. Pharmacists may be slow (temporarily unable to vote) *)
(* but the quorum tolerates that. Dispensed plus reserved units must never  *)
(* exceed the stocked capacity.                                             *)
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Reqs, Pharmacists, Quorum, Capacity

VARIABLES reqState, approvers, reserved, dispensed, pstate

vars == <<reqState, approvers, reserved, dispensed, pstate>>

TypeInv ==
    /\ reqState \in [Reqs -> {"pending", "approved", "dispensed", "denied"}]
    /\ approvers \in [Reqs -> SUBSET Pharmacists]
    /\ reserved \in 0..Capacity
    /\ dispensed \in 0..Capacity
    /\ pstate \in [Pharmacists -> {"ready", "slow"}]

Init ==
    /\ reqState = [r \in Reqs |-> "pending"]
    /\ approvers = [r \in Reqs |-> {}]
    /\ reserved = 0
    /\ dispensed = 0
    /\ pstate = [p \in Pharmacists |-> "ready"]

Vote(r, p) ==
    /\ reqState[r] = "pending"
    /\ pstate[p] = "ready"
    /\ p \notin approvers[r]
    /\ approvers' = [approvers EXCEPT ![r] = approvers[r] \cup {p}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reqState, reserved, dispensed, pstate>>

Reserve(r) ==
    /\ reqState[r] = "pending"
    /\ Cardinality(approvers[r]) >= Quorum
    /\ dispensed + reserved < Capacity
    /\ reqState' = [reqState EXCEPT ![r] = "approved"]
    /\ reserved' = reserved + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<approvers, dispensed, pstate>>

Dispense(r) ==
    /\ reqState[r] = "approved"
    /\ reqState' = [reqState EXCEPT ![r] = "dispensed"]
    /\ reserved' = reserved - 1
    /\ dispensed' = dispensed + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<approvers, pstate>>

Deny(r) ==
    /\ reqState[r] = "pending"
    /\ Cardinality(approvers[r]) < Quorum
    /\ reqState' = [reqState EXCEPT ![r] = "denied"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<approvers, reserved, dispensed, pstate>>

GoSlow(p) ==
    /\ pstate[p] = "ready"
    /\ pstate' = [pstate EXCEPT ![p] = "slow"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reqState, approvers, reserved, dispensed>>

Wake(p) ==
    /\ pstate[p] = "slow"
    /\ pstate' = [pstate EXCEPT ![p] = "ready"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reqState, approvers, reserved, dispensed>>

Next ==
    \/ \E r \in Reqs, p \in Pharmacists : Vote(r, p)
    \/ \E r \in Reqs : Reserve(r)
    \/ \E r \in Reqs : Dispense(r)
    \/ \E r \in Reqs : Deny(r)
    \/ \E p \in Pharmacists : GoSlow(p)
    \/ \E p \in Pharmacists : Wake(p)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

(* The units reserved plus the units already dispensed never exceed the    *)
(* pharmacy's stocked capacity.                                            *)
DispenseWithinStock == reserved + dispensed <= Capacity

Once a request has gathered a quorum of votes and there is still capacity in stock, a unit is reserved against that request and the request becomes approved. The pharmacy must never over-commit its shelf: the units currently reserved plus the units already dispensed can never exceed the stocked capacity.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od5m8p5t5 ---------------------------
(* A multiplayer game lobby matchmaker. Starting a match is irreversible and *)
(* must happen at most once per lobby. Normally a player takes a coarse      *)
(* region lock then a fine lobby lock (hierarchical locks) before starting.  *)
(* A privileged admin can override the locks and force a start. Each lobby   *)
(* holds a single start token that a start consumes.                         *)
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Players, Lobbies, LobbyRegionA, NoPlayer

ASSUME LobbyRegionA \subseteq Lobbies
ASSUME NoPlayer \notin Players

Regions == {"rg1", "rg2"}
LobbyRegion(lb) == IF lb \in LobbyRegionA THEN "rg1" ELSE "rg2"

VARIABLES regionLock, lobbyLock, started, tickets, pstate

vars == <<regionLock, lobbyLock, started, tickets, pstate>>

TypeInv ==
    /\ regionLock \in [Regions -> Players \cup {NoPlayer}]
    /\ lobbyLock \in [Lobbies -> Players \cup {NoPlayer}]
    /\ started \in [Lobbies -> BOOLEAN]
    /\ tickets \in [Lobbies -> 0..1]
    /\ pstate \in [Players -> {"idle", "hasRegion", "hasLobby"}]

Init ==
    /\ regionLock = [r \in Regions |-> NoPlayer]
    /\ lobbyLock = [lb \in Lobbies |-> NoPlayer]
    /\ started = [lb \in Lobbies |-> FALSE]
    /\ tickets = [lb \in Lobbies |-> 1]
    /\ pstate = [p \in Players |-> "idle"]

AcquireRegion(p, r) ==
    /\ pstate[p] = "idle"
    /\ regionLock[r] = NoPlayer
    /\ regionLock' = [regionLock EXCEPT ![r] = p]
    /\ pstate' = [pstate EXCEPT ![p] = "hasRegion"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lobbyLock, started, tickets>>

AcquireLobby(p, lb) ==
    /\ pstate[p] = "hasRegion"
    /\ regionLock[LobbyRegion(lb)] = p
    /\ lobbyLock[lb] = NoPlayer
    /\ lobbyLock' = [lobbyLock EXCEPT ![lb] = p]
    /\ pstate' = [pstate EXCEPT ![p] = "hasLobby"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<regionLock, started, tickets>>

StartMatch(p, lb) ==
    /\ pstate[p] = "hasLobby"
    /\ lobbyLock[lb] = p
    /\ started[lb] = FALSE
    /\ tickets[lb] >= 1
    /\ started' = [started EXCEPT ![lb] = TRUE]
    /\ tickets' = [tickets EXCEPT ![lb] = tickets[lb] - 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<regionLock, lobbyLock, pstate>>

ReleaseLocks(p, lb) ==
    /\ pstate[p] = "hasLobby"
    /\ lobbyLock[lb] = p
    /\ lobbyLock' = [lobbyLock EXCEPT ![lb] = NoPlayer]
    /\ regionLock' = [regionLock EXCEPT ![LobbyRegion(lb)] = NoPlayer]
    /\ pstate' = [pstate EXCEPT ![p] = "idle"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<started, tickets>>

AdminStart(lb) ==
    /\ started[lb] = FALSE
    /\ tickets[lb] >= 1
    /\ started' = [started EXCEPT ![lb] = TRUE]
    /\ tickets' = [tickets EXCEPT ![lb] = tickets[lb] - 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<regionLock, lobbyLock, pstate>>

Next ==
    \/ \E p \in Players, r \in Regions : AcquireRegion(p, r)
    \/ \E p \in Players, lb \in Lobbies : AcquireLobby(p, lb)
    \/ \E p \in Players, lb \in Lobbies : StartMatch(p, lb)
    \/ \E p \in Players, lb \in Lobbies : ReleaseLocks(p, lb)
    \/ \E lb \in Lobbies : AdminStart(lb)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

(* Each lobby's single start token is conserved: it is either still unused  *)
(* or has been consumed by exactly one match start, so a match starts at    *)
(* most once per lobby.                                                     *)
StartHappensAtMostOnce ==
    \A lb \in Lobbies :
        tickets[lb] + (IF started[lb] THEN 1 ELSE 0) = 1

=============================================================================
nl:
A multiplayer game lobby matchmaker must guarantee that starting a match, an irreversible action, happens at most once per lobby. Under the normal protocol a player uses hierarchical locks: it first takes a coarse lock on a region, then a fine lock on a specific lobby within that region, and only while holding the lobby lock may it start that lobby's match. Each lobby is created with a single start token; starting a match consumes the token and permanently marks the lobby as started, so a second start is impossible because the token is gone. When done, a player releases both the lobby and region locks. Separately, a privileged admin can override the locking protocol entirely and force a lobby to start, but this override still consumes the same single start token and so is likewise subject to the at-most-once rule. Whether started through the normal locks or by the admin override, a lobby's match can never be launched twice.
SAFETY PROPERTY: In every reachable state, each lobby's start token count plus one for whether it has started equals one, so no lobby's match is ever started more than once.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od5m7p0t1 ---------------------------
(* A multiplayer matchmaker guards each match slot with a compare-and-swap  *)
(* register. Players submit acquire requests that are processed in any      *)
(* order (messages can be reordered); a request succeeds only if the slot's *)
(* register is empty (the CAS expects empty), in which case the player      *)
(* enters the slot's critical section. The slot is a critical resource.     *)
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Players, Slots, Empty, MaxEpoch

ASSUME Empty \notin Players

VARIABLES reg, epoch, inCS, pending

vars == <<reg, epoch, inCS, pending>>

TypeInv ==
    /\ reg \in [Slots -> Players \cup {Empty}]
    /\ epoch \in [Slots -> 0..MaxEpoch]
    /\ inCS \in [Slots -> SUBSET Players]
    /\ pending \subseteq (Players \X Slots)

Init ==
    /\ reg = [s \in Slots |-> Empty]
    /\ epoch = [s \in Slots |-> 0]
    /\ inCS = [s \in Slots |-> {}]
    /\ pending = {}

Submit(p, s) ==
    /\ <<p, s>> \notin pending
    /\ p \notin inCS[s]
    /\ pending' = pending \cup {<<p, s>>}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, epoch, inCS>>

Process(p, s) ==
    /\ <<p, s>> \in pending
    /\ reg[s] = Empty
    /\ epoch[s] < MaxEpoch
    /\ reg' = [reg EXCEPT ![s] = p]
    /\ epoch' = [epoch EXCEPT ![s] = epoch[s] + 1]
    /\ inCS' = [inCS EXCEPT ![s] = inCS[s] \cup {p}]
    /\ pending' = pending \ {<<p, s>>}

Fail(p, s) ==
    /\ <<p, s>> \in pending
    /\ reg[s] # Empty
    /\ pending' = pending \ {<<p, s>>}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, epoch, inCS>>

Release(p, s) ==
    /\ reg[s] = p
    /\ reg' = [reg EXCEPT ![s] = Empty]
    /\ inCS' = [inCS EXCEPT ![s] = inCS[s] \ {p}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, pending>>

Next ==
    \/ \E p \in Players, s \in Slots : Submit(p, s)
    \/ \E p \in Players, s \in Slots : Process(p, s)
    \/ \E p \in Players, s \in Slots : Fail(p, s)
    \/ \E p \in Players, s \in Slots : Release(p, s)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

(* Each slot's critical section holds at most one player, and any player in *)
(* it is exactly the current owner recorded in the slot's CAS register.     *)
SlotMutualExclusion ==
    \A s \in Slots :
        /\ \A p1, p2 \in inCS[s] : p1 = p2
        /\ \A p \in inCS[s] : reg[s] = p

=============================================================================

A multiplayer game lobby matchmaker assigns players to match slots, protecting each slot with a compare-and-swap register that records the slot's current owner or a distinguished empty marker. Players submit acquire requests for slots, and because the underlying messaging is unordered, these requests are processed in an arbitrary order rather than the order submitted. When a request is processed, it performs a compare-and-swap that expects the slot's register to be empty: if it is, the register is set to the requesting player, the slot's version is bumped, and that player enters the slot's critical section. (* two-phase commit: the bag enters voting on a chosen chute, handlers vote *)
(* yes, and the bag commits only if all (non-crashed) handlers approved and *)
(* the chute is free. A handler can crash silently, never voting again,     *)
(* which blocks commit. A chute holds at most one bag at a time.            *)

ASSUME NoChute \notin Chutes

VARIABLES txnState, chuteOf, occupant, votes, crashed

TypeInv ==
    /\ txnState \in [Bags -> {"idle", "voting", "committed", "aborted"}]
    /\ chuteOf \in [Bags -> Chutes \cup {NoChute}]
    /\ occupant \in [Chutes -> SUBSET Bags]
    /\ votes \in [Bags -> SUBSET Handlers]
    /\ crashed \subseteq Handlers

Init ==
    /\ txnState = [b \in Bags |-> "idle"]
    /\ chuteOf = [b \in Bags |-> NoChute]
    /\ occupant = [c \in Chutes |-> {}]
    /\ votes = [b \in Bags |-> {}]
    /\ crashed = {}

Begin(b, c) ==
    /\ txnState[b] = "idle"
    /\ txnState' = [txnState EXCEPT ![b] = "voting"]
    /\ chuteOf' = [chuteOf EXCEPT ![b] = c]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<occupant, votes, crashed>>

Vote(b, h) ==
    /\ txnState[b] = "voting"
    /\ h \notin crashed
    /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![b] = votes[b] \cup {h}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<txnState, chuteOf, occupant, crashed>>

Commit(b) ==
    /\ txnState[b] = "voting"
    /\ votes[b] = Handlers
    /\ occupant[chuteOf[b]] = {}
    /\ txnState' = [txnState EXCEPT ![b] = "committed"]
    /\ occupant' = [occupant EXCEPT ![chuteOf[b]] = {b}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<chuteOf, votes, crashed>>

Abort(b) ==
    /\ txnState[b] = "voting"
    /\ votes[b] # Handlers
    /\ txnState' = [txnState EXCEPT ![b] = "aborted"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<chuteOf, occupant, votes, crashed>>

Vacate(b) ==
    /\ txnState[b] = "committed"
    /\ occupant' = [occupant EXCEPT ![chuteOf[b]] = occupant[chuteOf[b]] \ {b}]
    /\ txnState' = [txnState EXCEPT ![b] = "aborted"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<chuteOf, votes, crashed>>

CrashSilently(h) ==
    /\ h \notin crashed
    /\ crashed' = crashed \cup {h}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<txnState, chuteOf, occupant, votes>>

Next ==
    \/ \E b \in Bags, c \in Chutes : Begin(b, c)
    \/ \E b \in Bags, h \in Handlers : Vote(b, h)
    \/ \E b \in Bags : Commit(b)
    \/ \E b \in Bags : Abort(b)
    \/ \E b \in Bags : Vacate(b)
    \/ \E h \in Handlers : CrashSilently(h)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

(* No chute ever holds two bags at the same time.                          *)
ChuteExclusive == \A c \in Chutes : \A b1, b2 \in occupant[c] : b1 = b2

An airport baggage router decides which chute each bag is sent to, committing the assignment through a two-phase commit so that partial routing decisions are never left dangling. A bag begins by entering the voting phase on a chosen destination chute. The participating baggage handlers each vote to approve the routing. The bag commits only when every handler has voted to approve and the target chute is currently empty; committing places the bag in that chute. If approvals cannot all be gathered, the bag's transaction aborts and it is not placed. A handler can crash silently: it stops participating without warning and never casts another vote, which means any transaction still waiting on that handler can no longer commit and must abort. A committed bag eventually vacates its chute, freeing it for another bag. Because a chute is a physical resource, it must never hold two bags at once.
SAFETY PROPERTY: In every reachable state, each chute holds at most one bag at a time.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od1m8p3t3 ---------------------------
(* An air-traffic runway allocator uses hierarchical locks: a flight first  *)
(* takes a coarse lock on a runway, then allocates a fine (runway, time)    *)
(* slot on it. A flight may go slow while holding its runway lock. No two    *)
(* flights may ever be allocated the same slot.                             *)
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Flights, Runways, Times, NoFlight, NoRunway, NoSlot

ASSUME NoFlight \notin Flights
ASSUME NoRunway \notin Runways
ASSUME NoSlot \notin (Runways \X Times)

VARIABLES runwayLock, slotOf, fphase, heldRunway

vars == <<runwayLock, slotOf, fphase, heldRunway>>

TypeInv ==
    /\ runwayLock \in [Runways -> Flights \cup {NoFlight}]
    /\ slotOf \in [Flights -> (Runways \X Times) \cup {NoSlot}]
    /\ fphase \in [Flights -> {"idle", "hasRunway", "slow", "allocated"}]
    /\ heldRunway \in [Flights -> Runways \cup {NoRunway}]

Init ==
    /\ runwayLock = [r \in Runways |-> NoFlight]
    /\ slotOf = [f \in Flights |-> NoSlot]
    /\ fphase = [f \in Flights |-> "idle"]
    /\ heldRunway = [f \in Flights |-> NoRunway]

AcquireRunway(f, r) ==
    /\ fphase[f] = "idle"
    /\ runwayLock[r] = NoFlight
    /\ runwayLock' = [runwayLock EXCEPT ![r] = f]
    /\ fphase' = [fphase EXCEPT ![f] = "hasRunway"]
    /\ heldRunway' = [heldRunway EXCEPT ![f] = r]
    /\ UNCHANGED slotOf

GoSlow(f) ==
    /\ fphase[f] = "hasRunway"
    /\ fphase' = [fphase EXCEPT ![f] = "slow"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<runwayLock, slotOf, heldRunway>>

Allocate(f, t) ==
    /\ fphase[f] \in {"hasRunway", "slow"}
    /\ LET slot == <<heldRunway[f], t>> IN
        /\ \A g \in Flights : slotOf[g] # slot
        /\ slotOf' = [slotOf EXCEPT ![f] = slot]
    /\ fphase' = [fphase EXCEPT ![f] = "allocated"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<runwayLock, heldRunway>>

Release(f) ==
    /\ fphase[f] = "allocated"
    /\ runwayLock' = [runwayLock EXCEPT ![heldRunway[f]] = NoFlight]
    /\ slotOf' = [slotOf EXCEPT ![f] = NoSlot]
    /\ fphase' = [fphase EXCEPT ![f] = "idle"]
    /\ heldRunway' = [heldRunway EXCEPT ![f] = NoRunway]

Next ==
    \/ \E f \in Flights, r \in Runways : AcquireRunway(f, r)
    \/ \E f \in Flights : GoSlow(f)
    \/ \E f \in Flights, t \in Times : Allocate(f, t)
    \/ \E f \in Flights : Release(f)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

(* Slot allocation is injective across flights: two distinct flights are    *)
(* never allocated the very same (runway, time) slot.                       *)
NoDoubleSlotAllocation ==
    \A f1, f2 \in Flights :
        (slotOf[f1] # NoSlot /\ slotOf[f1] = slotOf[f2]) => f1 = f2

=============================================================================

CONSTANTS
    Flights = {f1, f2}
    Runways = {rwA, rwB}
    Times = {t1, t2}
    NoFlight = nofl
    NoRunway = norw
    NoSlot = nosl
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoDoubleSlotAllocation
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE

An air-traffic runway allocator hands out landing slots to flights using two levels of locking. A flight must first take a coarse lock on a whole runway; only one flight can hold a given runway lock at a time. Having secured a runway, the flight then allocates a fine-grained slot, which is a specific pairing of that runway with a landing time. A flight may become slow while holding its runway lock, delaying its own progress but not corrupting the protocol. A slot allocation succeeds only if no flight currently holds that exact (runway, time) slot. When the flight is finished it releases both its slot and its runway lock, freeing them for others. The central safety requirement is that the same landing slot is never handed to two different flights at once.
SAFETY PROPERTY: In every reachable state, no two distinct flights are allocated the same (runway, time) slot.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od8m0p2t4 ---------------------------
(* A university course-registration system with optimistic locking and a    *)
(* runtime-adjustable capacity. Physical seats are conserved: each seat is  *)
(* free, occupied by an enrollment, or held offline by the registrar. The   *)
(* registrar moves seats between free and offline at runtime. Students      *)
(* enroll optimistically, committing only if the version they read is still *)
(* current; every seat movement bumps the version.                          *)
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Students, TotalSeats, MaxVer

VARIABLES free, adminHeld, enrolledCount, version, token, sstate

vars == <<free, adminHeld, enrolledCount, version, token, sstate>>

TypeInv ==
    /\ free \in 0..TotalSeats
    /\ adminHeld \in 0..TotalSeats
    /\ enrolledCount \in 0..TotalSeats
    /\ version \in 0..MaxVer
    /\ token \in [Students -> 0..MaxVer]
    /\ sstate \in [Students -> {"idle", "read", "enrolled"}]

Init ==
    /\ free = TotalSeats
    /\ adminHeld = 0
    /\ enrolledCount = 0
    /\ version = 0
    /\ token = [s \in Students |-> 0]
    /\ sstate = [s \in Students |-> "idle"]

Read(s) ==
    /\ sstate[s] = "idle"
    /\ sstate' = [sstate EXCEPT ![s] = "read"]
    /\ token' = [token EXCEPT ![s] = version]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<free, adminHeld, enrolledCount, version>>

Enroll(s) ==
    /\ sstate[s] = "read"
    /\ token[s] = version
    /\ version < MaxVer
    /\ free >= 1
    /\ free' = free - 1
    /\ enrolledCount' = enrolledCount + 1
    /\ version' = version + 1
    /\ sstate' = [sstate EXCEPT ![s] = "enrolled"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<adminHeld, token>>

Retry(s) ==
    /\ sstate[s] = "read"
    /\ token[s] # version
    /\ sstate' = [sstate EXCEPT ![s] = "idle"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<free, adminHeld, enrolledCount, version, token>>

TakeOffline ==
    /\ free >= 1
    /\ version < MaxVer
    /\ free' = free - 1
    /\ adminHeld' = adminHeld + 1
    /\ version' = version + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<enrolledCount, token, sstate>>

BringOnline ==
    /\ adminHeld >= 1
    /\ version < MaxVer
    /\ adminHeld' = adminHeld - 1
    /\ free' = free + 1
    /\ version' = version + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<enrolledCount, token, sstate>>

Drop(s) ==
    /\ sstate[s] = "enrolled"
    /\ version < MaxVer
    /\ enrolledCount' = enrolledCount - 1
    /\ free' = free + 1
    /\ version' = version + 1
    /\ sstate' = [sstate EXCEPT ![s] = "idle"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<adminHeld, token>>

Next ==
    \/ \E s \in Students : Read(s)
    \/ \E s \in Students : Enroll(s)
    \/ \E s \in Students : Retry(s)
    \/ TakeOffline
    \/ BringOnline
    \/ \E s \in Students : Drop(s)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

(* Seats are conserved: free seats, occupied seats, and offline seats       *)
(* always sum to the fixed physical total, even as capacity is adjusted.    *)
SeatConservation == free + enrolledCount + adminHeld = TotalSeats

=============================================================================

CONSTANTS
    Students = {a, b}
    TotalSeats = 2
    MaxVer = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT SeatConservation
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A university course-registration system manages a fixed number of physical seats using optimistic locking, while letting the registrar adjust how many seats are open at runtime. Every seat is always in exactly one of three states: free and open for enrollment, occupied by an enrolled student, or held offline by the registrar. A student enrolls optimistically: it first reads the current version stamp, and later commits an enrollment only if that stamp is still current and a free seat remains, taking one free seat into occupancy. If the version has moved on, the read is stale and the student retries. The registrar can take a free seat offline or bring an offline seat back, and students can drop their enrollment, returning a seat to the free pool. Every one of these seat movements bumps the version stamp, which is what invalidates stale optimistic reads. Although the number of open seats changes over time, seats are never conjured or lost.
SAFETY PROPERTY: In every reachable state, the number of free seats plus occupied seats plus offline-held seats equals the fixed physical total, so no seat is ever created or destroyed.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od2m4p0t3 ---------------------------
(* A warehouse robot fleet pulls tasks from a bounded work queue (with      *)
(* backpressure when full) and shares a single charging station. The        *)
(* charging station is a critical resource: only one robot may be charging  *)
(* at a time. A working robot may go slow and later resume.                 *)
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Tasks, Robots, MaxQ, NoTask

ASSUME NoTask \notin Tasks

VARIABLES taskQueue, charging, rstate, assigned, doneTasks

vars == <<taskQueue, charging, rstate, assigned, doneTasks>>

TypeInv ==
    /\ taskQueue \subseteq Tasks
    /\ charging \subseteq Robots
    /\ rstate \in [Robots -> {"idle", "working", "slow", "charging"}]
    /\ assigned \in [Robots -> Tasks \cup {NoTask}]
    /\ doneTasks \subseteq Tasks

Init ==
    /\ taskQueue = {}
    /\ charging = {}
    /\ rstate = [r \in Robots |-> "idle"]
    /\ assigned = [r \in Robots |-> NoTask]
    /\ doneTasks = {}

Enqueue(k) ==
    /\ k \notin taskQueue
    /\ k \notin doneTasks
    /\ \A r \in Robots : assigned[r] # k
    /\ Cardinality(taskQueue) < MaxQ
    /\ taskQueue' = taskQueue \cup {k}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<charging, rstate, assigned, doneTasks>>

Claim(r, k) ==
    /\ rstate[r] = "idle"
    /\ k \in taskQueue
    /\ taskQueue' = taskQueue \ {k}
    /\ assigned' = [assigned EXCEPT ![r] = k]
    /\ rstate' = [rstate EXCEPT ![r] = "working"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<charging, doneTasks>>

Complete(r) ==
    /\ rstate[r] = "working"
    /\ doneTasks' = doneTasks \cup {assigned[r]}
    /\ assigned' = [assigned EXCEPT ![r] = NoTask]
    /\ rstate' = [rstate EXCEPT ![r] = "idle"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<taskQueue, charging>>

GoSlow(r) ==
    /\ rstate[r] = "working"
    /\ rstate' = [rstate EXCEPT ![r] = "slow"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<taskQueue, charging, assigned, doneTasks>>

Resume(r) ==
    /\ rstate[r] = "slow"
    /\ rstate' = [rstate EXCEPT ![r] = "working"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<taskQueue, charging, assigned, doneTasks>>

Charge(r) ==
    /\ rstate[r] = "idle"
    /\ charging = {}
    /\ charging' = {r}
    /\ rstate' = [rstate EXCEPT ![r] = "charging"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<taskQueue, assigned, doneTasks>>

Unplug(r) ==
    /\ r \in charging
    /\ charging' = charging \ {r}
    /\ rstate' = [rstate EXCEPT ![r] = "idle"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<taskQueue, assigned, doneTasks>>

Next ==
    \/ \E k \in Tasks : Enqueue(k)
    \/ \E r \in Robots, k \in Tasks : Claim(r, k)
    \/ \E r \in Robots : Complete(r)
    \/ \E r \in Robots : GoSlow(r)
    \/ \E r \in Robots : Resume(r)
    \/ \E r \in Robots : Charge(r)
    \/ \E r \in Robots : Unplug(r)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

(* At most one robot occupies the shared charging station at any time.      *)
ChargerExclusive == \A r1, r2 \in charging : r1 = r2

=============================================================================

CONSTANTS
    Tasks = {k1, k2, k3}
    Robots = {r1, r2}
    MaxQ = 2
    NoTask = notk
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT ChargerExclusive
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A warehouse robot fleet is fed work through a bounded task queue and shares a single charging station. New tasks are appended to the queue, but the queue applies backpressure: once it is full, further tasks cannot be enqueued until space frees up. An idle robot claims a task from the queue, removing it, and begins working; when it finishes, the task is recorded as done and the robot returns to idle. While working, a robot may go slow for a while and then resume, modelling a participant that is delayed but not failed. Separately, an idle robot may plug into the charging station, but only when no other robot is currently charging; the charging station is a physical resource that just one robot can use at a time. A charging robot later unplugs and becomes idle again. The fleet must never let two robots occupy the charging station simultaneously.
SAFETY PROPERTY: In every reachable state, at most one robot occupies the shared charging station.

--------------------------- MODULE W4Od12m1p5t4 ---------------------------
(* A blood-bank inventory tracker grants exclusive issuing rights via a     *)
(* token ring: a single token circulates among nodes and only the current   *)
(* token holder may issue a unit. Issuing a specific unit is irreversible    *)
(* and must happen at most once; each unit carries a single-use seal that    *)
(* an issue consumes. Available stock capacity changes at runtime.          *)
EXTENDS Integers, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Units, MaxStock

Nodes == {"n1", "n2", "n3"}
NextNode(x) ==
    CASE x = "n1" -> "n2"
      [] x = "n2" -> "n3"
      [] x = "n3" -> "n1"

VARIABLES holder, issuedSet, seal, stock

vars == <<holder, issuedSet, seal, stock>>

TypeInv ==
    /\ holder \in Nodes
    /\ issuedSet \subseteq Units
    /\ seal \in [Units -> -1..1]
    /\ stock \in 0..MaxStock

Init ==
    /\ holder = "n1"
    /\ issuedSet = {}
    /\ seal = [u \in Units |-> 1]
    /\ stock = MaxStock

PassToken ==
    /\ holder' = NextNode(holder)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<issuedSet, seal, stock>>

Issue(n, u) ==
    /\ n = holder
    /\ seal[u] = 1
    /\ stock >= 1
    /\ issuedSet' = issuedSet \cup {u}
    /\ seal' = [seal EXCEPT ![u] = seal[u] - 1]
    /\ stock' = stock - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED holder

Restock ==
    /\ stock < MaxStock
    /\ stock' = stock + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, issuedSet, seal>>

Spoil ==
    /\ stock >= 1
    /\ stock' = stock - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, issuedSet, seal>>

Next ==
    \/ PassToken
    \/ \E n \in Nodes, u \in Units : Issue(n, u)
    \/ Restock
    \/ Spoil

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

(* For every unit, its issued-record and its remaining single-use seal are  *)
(* complementary, summing to one: a unit is issued at most once.            *)
IssuedAtMostOnce ==
    \A u \in Units :
        (IF u \in issuedSet THEN 1 ELSE 0) + seal[u] = 1

=============================================================================

CONSTANTS
    Units = {u1, u2, u3}
    MaxStock = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT IssuedAtMostOnce
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A blood-bank inventory tracker coordinates several nodes that all want to issue blood units, but grants exclusive issuing rights using a token ring. A single token circulates around the ring of nodes, moving from each node to the next, and only the node currently holding the token is allowed to issue a unit. Issuing a particular unit is an irreversible action that must happen at most once: each unit carries a single-use seal, and issuing the unit consumes that seal and records the unit as issued. Because the seal is single-use, a unit that has already been issued can never be issued again. The bank's available stock capacity changes at runtime as fresh units are restocked and as units spoil and are discarded. The safety concern is that no unit is ever issued twice: for each unit, being recorded as issued and still holding its unused seal are mutually exclusive and together account for exactly one seal per unit.
SAFETY PROPERTY: In every reachable state, for each unit the indicator of whether it has been issued plus its remaining single-use seal count equals one, so no unit is ever issued more than once.

--------------------------- MODULE W4Od13m4p2t3 ---------------------------
(* A vending machine network buffers vend requests in a bounded work queue  *)
(* (backpressure when full) and conserves cans: every can is either in      *)
(* machine stock, in transit during a vend, or already dispensed. Machines  *)
(* may be slow but not failed.                                              *)
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Requests, Machines, MaxQ, TotalCans

VARIABLES requestQueue, servedReqs, stock, inTransit, dispensed, mstate

vars == <<requestQueue, servedReqs, stock, inTransit, dispensed, mstate>>

TypeInv ==
    /\ requestQueue \subseteq Requests
    /\ servedReqs \subseteq Requests
    /\ stock \in 0..TotalCans
    /\ inTransit \in 0..TotalCans
    /\ dispensed \in 0..TotalCans
    /\ mstate \in [Machines -> {"ready", "slow"}]

Init ==
    /\ requestQueue = {}
    /\ servedReqs = {}
    /\ stock = TotalCans
    /\ inTransit = 0
    /\ dispensed = 0
    /\ mstate = [m \in Machines |-> "ready"]

SubmitReq(q) ==
    /\ q \notin requestQueue
    /\ q \notin servedReqs
    /\ Cardinality(requestQueue) < MaxQ
    /\ requestQueue' = requestQueue \cup {q}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<servedReqs, stock, inTransit, dispensed, mstate>>

StartVend(m, q) ==
    /\ mstate[m] = "ready"
    /\ q \in requestQueue
    /\ stock >= 1
    /\ requestQueue' = requestQueue \ {q}
    /\ servedReqs' = servedReqs \cup {q}
    /\ stock' = stock - 1
    /\ inTransit' = inTransit + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<dispensed, mstate>>

DropCan ==
    /\ inTransit >= 1
    /\ inTransit' = inTransit - 1
    /\ dispensed' = dispensed + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<requestQueue, servedReqs, stock, mstate>>

GoSlow(m) ==
    /\ mstate[m] = "ready"
    /\ mstate' = [mstate EXCEPT ![m] = "slow"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<requestQueue, servedReqs, stock, inTransit, dispensed>>

Wake(m) ==
    /\ mstate[m] = "slow"
    /\ mstate' = [mstate EXCEPT ![m] = "ready"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<requestQueue, servedReqs, stock, inTransit, dispensed>>

Next ==
    \/ \E q \in Requests : SubmitReq(q)
    \/ \E m \in Machines, q \in Requests : StartVend(m, q)
    \/ DropCan
    \/ \E m \in Machines : GoSlow(m)
    \/ \E m \in Machines : Wake(m)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

(* Cans are conserved across the network: stock, in-transit, and dispensed  *)
(* cans always sum to the fixed total.                                      *)
CanConservation == stock + inTransit + dispensed = TotalCans

=============================================================================

    Machines = {m1, m2}
    MaxQ = 2
    TotalCans = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next

CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE

Incoming vend requests are appended to the queue, which applies backpressure and refuses new requests while it is full. A machine that is ready picks a queued request, removes it from the queue, marks it served, takes one can out of stock, and puts that can in transit as it is being vended. When the mechanism finishes, the in-transit can is dropped to the customer and counted as dispensed. A machine may be slow, temporarily unable to start new vends, but it never fails and can wake up and resume later. Across the whole network the population of cans is fixed: every can is at all times either sitting in stock, in transit through an active vend, or already dispensed, and cans are never manufactured or lost by the process.
SAFETY PROPERTY: In every reachable state, the number of cans in stock plus cans in transit plus cans dispensed equals the fixed total number of cans, so cans are neither created nor destroyed.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od1m4p3t5 ---------------------------
(* An air-traffic runway allocator queues landing requests in a bounded     *)
(* work queue and assigns each waiting flight a distinct landing slot. A     *)
(* privileged admin override can preempt a slot's current owner and force   *)
(* it onto another flight (evicting the prior owner). No slot is ever        *)
(* allocated to two flights at once.                                        *)
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Flights, Slots, MaxQ, MaxAdmin, NoSlot

ASSUME NoSlot \notin Slots

VARIABLES requestQueue, assignedSlot, fstate, adminBudget

vars == <<requestQueue, assignedSlot, fstate, adminBudget>>

TypeInv ==
    /\ requestQueue \subseteq Flights
    /\ assignedSlot \in [Flights -> Slots \cup {NoSlot}]
    /\ fstate \in [Flights -> {"idle", "waiting", "assigned", "landed"}]
    /\ adminBudget \in 0..MaxAdmin

Init ==
    /\ requestQueue = {}
    /\ assignedSlot = [f \in Flights |-> NoSlot]
    /\ fstate = [f \in Flights |-> "idle"]
    /\ adminBudget = MaxAdmin

Request(f) ==
    /\ fstate[f] = "idle"
    /\ Cardinality(requestQueue) < MaxQ
    /\ requestQueue' = requestQueue \cup {f}
    /\ fstate' = [fstate EXCEPT ![f] = "waiting"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<assignedSlot, adminBudget>>

Allocate(f, s) ==
    /\ fstate[f] = "waiting"
    /\ f \in requestQueue
    /\ \A g \in Flights : assignedSlot[g] # s
    /\ requestQueue' = requestQueue \ {f}
    /\ assignedSlot' = [assignedSlot EXCEPT ![f] = s]
    /\ fstate' = [fstate EXCEPT ![f] = "assigned"]
    /\ UNCHANGED adminBudget

AdminOverride(f, s) ==
    /\ fstate[f] = "waiting"
    /\ f \in requestQueue
    /\ adminBudget >= 1
    /\ requestQueue' = requestQueue \ {f}
    /\ assignedSlot' = [g \in Flights |->
            IF g = f THEN s
            ELSE IF assignedSlot[g] = s THEN NoSlot
            ELSE assignedSlot[g]]
    /\ fstate' = [g \in Flights |->
            IF g = f THEN "assigned"
            ELSE IF assignedSlot[g] = s THEN "idle"
            ELSE fstate[g]]
    /\ adminBudget' = adminBudget - 1

Land(f) ==
    /\ fstate[f] = "assigned"
    /\ fstate' = [fstate EXCEPT ![f] = "landed"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<requestQueue, assignedSlot, adminBudget>>

Release(f) ==
    /\ fstate[f] = "landed"
    /\ assignedSlot' = [assignedSlot EXCEPT ![f] = NoSlot]
    /\ fstate' = [fstate EXCEPT ![f] = "idle"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<requestQueue, adminBudget>>

Next ==
    \/ \E f \in Flights : Request(f)
    \/ \E f \in Flights, s \in Slots : Allocate(f, s)
    \/ \E f \in Flights, s \in Slots : AdminOverride(f, s)
    \/ \E f \in Flights : Land(f)
    \/ \E f \in Flights : Release(f)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

(* No landing slot is ever allocated to two distinct flights simultaneously *)
(* -- even after an admin override, which evicts the prior owner.           *)
NoDoubleSlot ==
    \A f1, f2 \in Flights :
        (assignedSlot[f1] # NoSlot /\ assignedSlot[f1] = assignedSlot[f2]) => f1 = f2

    MaxAdmin = 1
    NoSlot = nosl
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoDoubleSlot
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE

An air-traffic runway allocator receives landing requests into a bounded work queue that refuses new requests once it is full. Each waiting flight is eventually assigned a landing slot, and a normal assignment succeeds only if the chosen slot is not currently held by any flight, guaranteeing that a slot goes to just one flight. Once assigned, a flight lands and later releases its slot, returning it to the pool. The tower also has a privileged admin override: it can force a waiting flight onto a particular slot even if that slot is already taken, but doing so preempts and evicts the previous owner, sending that flight back to idle so the slot still ends up held by exactly one flight. The admin override is rationed by a small budget. The core requirement is that at no point is a single landing slot allocated to two different flights.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od4m4p0t4 ---------------------------
(* A car-wash conveyor line queues arriving cars in a bounded work queue     *)
(* (backpressure when full) and feeds them into wash bays. Each bay is a    *)
(* critical resource holding at most one car. Bays open and close at        *)
(* runtime, changing capacity; a bay can only close when empty.            *)
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Cars, Bays, MaxQ

VARIABLES carQueue, inBay, openBays, cstate

vars == <<carQueue, inBay, openBays, cstate>>

TypeInv ==
    /\ carQueue \subseteq Cars
    /\ inBay \in [Bays -> SUBSET Cars]
    /\ openBays \subseteq Bays
    /\ cstate \in [Cars -> {"idle", "waiting", "washing", "done"}]

Init ==
    /\ carQueue = {}
    /\ inBay = [b \in Bays |-> {}]
    /\ openBays = Bays
    /\ cstate = [c \in Cars |-> "idle"]

Arrive(c) ==
    /\ cstate[c] = "idle"
    /\ Cardinality(carQueue) < MaxQ
    /\ carQueue' = carQueue \cup {c}
    /\ cstate' = [cstate EXCEPT ![c] = "waiting"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<inBay, openBays>>

Enter(c, b) ==
    /\ cstate[c] = "waiting"
    /\ c \in carQueue
    /\ b \in openBays
    /\ inBay[b] = {}
    /\ carQueue' = carQueue \ {c}
    /\ inBay' = [inBay EXCEPT ![b] = {c}]
    /\ cstate' = [cstate EXCEPT ![c] = "washing"]
    /\ UNCHANGED openBays

Exit(c, b) ==
    /\ c \in inBay[b]
    /\ inBay' = [inBay EXCEPT ![b] = inBay[b] \ {c}]
    /\ cstate' = [cstate EXCEPT ![c] = "done"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<carQueue, openBays>>

OpenBay(b) ==
    /\ b \notin openBays
    /\ openBays' = openBays \cup {b}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<carQueue, inBay, cstate>>

CloseBay(b) ==
    /\ b \in openBays
    /\ inBay[b] = {}
    /\ openBays' = openBays \ {b}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<carQueue, inBay, cstate>>

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Cars : Arrive(c)
    \/ \E c \in Cars, b \in Bays : Enter(c, b)
    \/ \E c \in Cars, b \in Bays : Exit(c, b)
    \/ \E b \in Bays : OpenBay(b)
    \/ \E b \in Bays : CloseBay(b)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

(* Each wash bay holds at most one car, and any occupied bay is open.       *)
BayExclusive ==
    \A b \in Bays :
        /\ \A c1, c2 \in inBay[b] : c1 = c2
        /\ inBay[b] # {} => b \in openBays

=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Cars = {c1, c2, c3}
    Bays = {b1, b2}
    MaxQ = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT BayExclusive
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A car-wash conveyor line manages arriving cars and a set of wash bays. Arriving cars join a bounded work queue, which applies backpressure and turns away new arrivals while it is full. A waiting car enters a wash bay only if that bay is currently open and empty; entering removes the car from the queue and places it in the bay to be washed. When the wash finishes, the car exits the bay and the bay becomes empty again. The line's capacity changes at runtime because bays can be opened and closed for maintenance, but a bay may only be closed while it is empty so that no in-progress wash is disrupted. Because each bay physically fits a single car, a bay must never contain two cars at once, and any bay that has a car in it must be open.
SAFETY PROPERTY: In every reachable state, each wash bay holds at most one car, and any bay that is occupied is currently open.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od4m9p2t4 ---------------------------
(* A car-wash conveyor line that reconfigures its capacity through          *)
(* epoch-numbered reconfigurations. Cars are conserved across reconfigs:    *)
(* every car is waiting to board, on the conveyor, or exited. A             *)
(* reconfiguration changes the conveyor capacity (tagged by a new epoch)    *)
(* but is never allowed to shrink below the cars currently on the line.     *)
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS TotalCars, MaxCap, MaxEpoch

VARIABLES epoch, onLine, waiting, exited, capacity

vars == <<epoch, onLine, waiting, exited, capacity>>

TypeInv ==
    /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
    /\ onLine \in 0..TotalCars
    /\ waiting \in 0..TotalCars
    /\ exited \in 0..TotalCars
    /\ capacity \in 0..MaxCap

Init ==
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ onLine = 0
    /\ waiting = TotalCars
    /\ exited = 0
    /\ capacity = MaxCap

Board ==
    /\ waiting >= 1
    /\ onLine < capacity
    /\ waiting' = waiting - 1
    /\ onLine' = onLine + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, exited, capacity>>

ExitLine ==
    /\ onLine >= 1
    /\ onLine' = onLine - 1
    /\ exited' = exited + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, waiting, capacity>>

Recycle ==
    /\ exited >= 1
    /\ exited' = exited - 1
    /\ waiting' = waiting + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, onLine, capacity>>

Reconfigure(newcap) ==
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ newcap \in 0..MaxCap
    /\ newcap >= onLine
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ capacity' = newcap
    /\ UNCHANGED <<onLine, waiting, exited>>

Next ==
    \/ Board
    \/ ExitLine
    \/ Recycle
    \/ \E newcap \in 0..MaxCap : Reconfigure(newcap)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

(* Cars are conserved across all reconfigurations: waiting, on-line, and    *)
(* exited cars always sum to the fixed total.                              *)
CarConservation == waiting + onLine + exited = TotalCars

=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    TotalCars = 2
    MaxCap = 2
    MaxEpoch = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT CarConservation
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A car-wash conveyor line periodically reconfigures how many cars it can carry, using epoch-numbered reconfigurations so each change of capacity is tagged with a fresh epoch. Cars progress through three stages: waiting to board, riding on the conveyor, and exited after washing. A waiting car boards only when the conveyor is below its current capacity, moving from waiting to on-line. A car on the conveyor eventually reaches the end and exits. An exited car may recycle back into the waiting stage for another pass. When the operator reconfigures the line, the epoch advances and the capacity is set to a new value, but the reconfiguration is forbidden from shrinking capacity below the number of cars currently on the conveyor, so no car is ever pushed off. Throughout all of this, the fleet of cars is fixed: no matter how the conveyor is reconfigured, every car is always accounted for as waiting, on-line, or exited.
SAFETY PROPERTY: In every reachable state, the number of waiting cars plus on-line cars plus exited cars equals the fixed total, so reconfiguration never creates or destroys a car.
